title: BTC to XMR: Can You Send Lightning Bitcoin to an On-Chain Deposit?
keyQuestions: Can a Lightning wallet send to a normal Bitcoin address?
How do I know whether a BTC deposit is on-chain or Lightning?
Can Lightning BTC directly fund a BTC to XMR order?
What is the difference between a Lightning invoice and a Bitcoin address?
What should I check when a wallet offers a swap-out?
What should I do after using the wrong Bitcoin payment rail?
quickSteps: Identify the deposit rail by reading the network label and payment type on the active order.
Confirm the wallet's send mode and make sure it will create an on-chain Bitcoin transaction, not a Lightning payment.
Convert or withdraw Lightning funds on-chain first when the wallet cannot pay the requested address directly.
Create a fresh BTC to XMR order only after the required amount is spendable on-chain and the Monero address is verified.
Verify the destination, amount, fee, and on-chain TXID before treating the deposit as sent, and stop if any detail does not match.

issueRouting.start: A BTC to XMR order requests an on-chain Bitcoin deposit, but the user's BTC may be on Lightning.

branches.if: The wallet has enough spendable on-chain BTC.
then: Select the wallet's on-chain Bitcoin account.
Confirm that the order requests the Bitcoin mainnet payment rail.
Review the destination and amount before sending.

branches.if: The balance is on Lightning and the wallet offers a swap-out.
then: Review the conversion provider, fees, limits, output amount, and timing.
Move the funds to an on-chain wallet controlled by the user.
Wait until the resulting BTC is spendable before creating a fresh order.

branches.if: A payment was already attempted through the wrong rail.
then: Determine whether the payment failed, created an on-chain TXID, or completed as a Lightning payment.
Collect the order ID, destination, amount, time, status, and payment identifier.
Contact the relevant service through its official channel and do not send a second payment.

riskNotes: A native Lightning payment does not create the on-chain transaction expected by an ordinary Bitcoin deposit address.
A combined BTC balance can hide how much is actually spendable on-chain.
A swap-out may deduct conversion and network fees from the amount that reaches the on-chain destination.
Scanning a QR code successfully does not prove that the wallet selected the correct payment rail.
A seed phrase, private key, wallet backup, password, or remote-access session must never be shared for payment recovery.
